### Step 1 — Import & Inspect the original SAS datasets


Find the original SAS datasets in AllQsbyQ and import them into R for inspection.  There should be one dataset for the self-reports completed by children and another for reports completed by their parents.




```{r import-data}

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(misty)



CHILD_RAW <- read_sas("/Volumes/FDrive/AllQsbyQ/HIPIC/allhipic_c.sas7bdat")
PARENT_RAW <- read_sas("/Volumes/FDrive/AllQsbyQ/HIPIC/allhipic_p.sas7bdat")

```

## A. Initial Data Quality Assessment

Before making any modifications, we examine the original datasets
for missing values. This establishes a baseline against which
subsequent exclusions and imputations can be verified.




```{r inspect-missingness, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Dimensions of the original datasets
dim(CHILD_RAW)
dim(PARENT_RAW)

# Total missing values across all variables
sum(is.na(CHILD_RAW))
sum(is.na(PARENT_RAW))

cat("The CHILD dataset contains", nrow(CHILD_RAW),
    "observations and", ncol(CHILD_RAW), "variables.\n")


cat("The PARENT dataset contains", nrow(PARENT_RAW),
    "observations and", ncol(PARENT_RAW), "variables.\n")



# Number of observations containing at least one missing value
sum(!complete.cases(CHILD_RAW))
sum(!complete.cases(PARENT_RAW))


library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)

CHILD_MISSING <- CHILD_RAW %>%
  mutate(N_MISSING = rowSums(is.na(pick(11:154)))) %>%
  filter(N_MISSING > 0) %>%
  select(ID4, DOE, N_MISSING)


PARENT_MISSING <- PARENT_RAW %>%
  mutate(N_MISSING = rowSums(is.na(pick(13:156)))) %>%
  filter(N_MISSING > 0) %>%
  select(ID4, DOE, N_MISSING)


#rowSums(is.na(dplyr::select(CHILD_RAW, starts_with("HC"))))
#rowSums(is.na(dplyr::select(PARENT_RAW, starts_with("HP"))))

```


## B. Remove Disqualified Observations

Any observation from both the Child and Parent datasets where a substantial portion of the survey was unanswered (approx. gt 1%). For remaining observations with NA values in select questions, use a simply mean substitution, where the rounded average for that question by nutritional group + sex (CVPK + MVF) serves as a proxy for missing values.


``` {r mean-substitution}


library(magrittr)


# excluding by subsetting from values in a datatable

# CHILD_EXCLUDE <- subset(CHILD_MISSING, N_MISSING > 3  | is.na(DOE) , select = ID4)
# PARENT_EXCLUDE <- subset(PARENT_MISSING, N_MISSING > 3 | is.na(DOE) , select = ID4)
# 
# 
# CHILD <-  CHILD_RAW %>% subset(!(ID4 %in% CHILD_EXCLUDE$ID4))
# PARENT <- PARENT_RAW %>% subset(!(ID4 %in% PARENT_EXCLUDE$ID4))
# 


# excluding based on values in a vector


CHILD_EXCLUDE <- CHILD_MISSING %>% filter( N_MISSING >= 3 | is.na(DOE)) %>% pull(ID4)
PARENT_EXCLUDE <- PARENT_MISSING %>% filter( N_MISSING >= 3 | is.na(DOE)) %>% pull(ID4)


CHILD <-  CHILD_RAW %>% filter( !ID4 %in% CHILD_EXCLUDE)
PARENT <- PARENT_RAW %>% filter( !ID4 %in% PARENT_EXCLUDE)



#use the GROUPBY and ACROSS functions to find the CVPK/MVF mean and then apply those to questions that are missing:


CHILD <- CHILD %>%
  group_by(CVPK, MVF) %>%
  mutate(across(last_col(offset = 143):last_col(),
                function(x) {
                  ifelse(is.na(x),
                         round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                         x)
                })) %>%
  ungroup()



PARENT <- PARENT %>%
  group_by(CVPK, MVF) %>%
  mutate(across(last_col(offset = 143):last_col(),
                function(x) {
                  ifelse(is.na(x),
                         round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                         x)
                })) %>%
  ungroup()



#Confirm no missing values .....

sum(!complete.cases(CHILD))
sum(!complete.cases(PARENT))



```


## C.  Examine Cohort Demographic Data - ensure that the nutritional groups are reasonably balanced and that there isn't a statistically significant differece between them along demographic characteristics that might be used in later analyses.


``` {r cohort-demographics}


demog <-   
    
  
function(DATA) {
  
  
  temp <- deparse(substitute(DATA));
  DSN <- get(paste0(temp, "_RAW"))  

#  MDSN <-  get(paste0(str_sub(temp,1,1), "MISS"))
  
  #Goodness of Fit
  
  cat("\n====", "Goodness of Fit (Before)", "====\n")
  DSN %>% select(CVPK) %>% table() %>%  rstatix::chisq_test(., p= c(0.5, 0.5)) %>% print(.)
  
  
  #Missingness
  
  MDSN <- DSN %>%
    select(ID4, CVPK, last_col(offset=143) : last_col()) %>%
    rowwise() %>% 
    mutate(MISSING = sum(is.na(c_across(last_col(offset = 143):last_col())))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(MISSING >= 3) %>%
    select(ID4, CVPK, MISSING) 
  
  
  cat("\n====", "Exclusions by Nutritional Group", "====\n")

  EXCL_TAB <- DSN %>%
    mutate(EXCLUDED = ID4 %in% pull(MDSN, ID4)) %$%
    table(CVPK, EXCLUDED)

  print(EXCL_TAB)                                         # counts
  print(round(100 * prop.table(EXCL_TAB, margin = 1), 1)) # row %: % excluded per group
  print(fisher.test(EXCL_TAB))                            # the p-value for the table
  
  
  
  
  
  
  cat("\n====", "Goodness of Fit (After)", "====\n")
  
  cat("Excluded for >= 3 missing items:", nrow(MDSN), "\n")
  
  ANALYSIS <-  DSN %>% anti_join( MDSN[, c("ID4")], by="ID4") %>% select(ID4, CVPK, MVF, AGEEXAM) 
            
  ANALYSIS %>% select (CVPK) %>% table() %>% rstatix::chisq_test(., p= c(0.5, 0.5)) %>% print()
    
  
  # Mean Nutritional Groups
  
  cat("\n====", "Mean Age by Nutritional Group", "====\n")
  DSN %>% filter(!ID4 %in% pull(MDSN, ID4))  %>%                 #PRESERVED FOR EDUC PURPOSES - ALT METHOD
    misty::test.welch( AGEEXAM ~ CVPK, data = .,  descript=T)  
    
  
  
  
  # Percent Male
  
  
  cat("\n====", "Percentage of Male Subjects by Nutritional Group", "====\n")
  ANALYSIS %$% 
    sjPlot::plot_xtab(CVPK, MVF, margin = "row",
                      bar.pos = "stack", coord.flip = F,
                      title = "Sex Distribution by Nutritional Group",
                      axis.titles = c("CVPK"),
                      legend.title = "Sex",
                      geom.colors = c("#006cc5", "#cbcccb"),
                      show.summary = TRUE) %>% print(.)
  
  
   PCT <-  
   ANALYSIS  %$% 
    chisq.test(CVPK, MVF, correct = F) %>% .$observed %T>% print() %>% prop.table(margin = 1) %>% round(3) *100 
   
   print(PCT)
 
   ANALYSIS %$% chisq.test(CVPK, MVF, correct = F) %>% print()
  
   
   
   # ---- Summary table: MAL (1) first, CON (0) second ----

  orig_n  <- table(DSN$CVPK)                     # original N per group
  final_n <- table(ANALYSIS$CVPK)                # final N per group
  excl_n  <- EXCL_TAB[, "TRUE"]                  # excluded per group
  male_n  <- table(ANALYSIS$CVPK, ANALYSIS$MVF)[, "0"]   # MVF 0 = male

  age_txt <- sapply(c("1", "0"), function(g) {
    x <- ANALYSIS$AGEEXAM[ANALYSIS$CVPK == as.numeric(g)]
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x))
  })

  fmt_p <- function(p) sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))   # 0.4487 -> ".449"

  col_for <- function(g) {
    c(orig_n[g],
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", excl_n[g], 100 * excl_n[g] / orig_n[g]),
      final_n[g],
      age_txt[g],
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", male_n[g], 100 * male_n[g] / final_n[g]))
  }

  TAB <- tibble(
    ` ` = c("Original N", ">2% of items missing, n (%)", "Final analytic N",
            "Testing age, years, mean (SD)", "Male, n (%)"),
    MAL = unname(col_for("1")),
    CON = unname(col_for("0")),
    p   = c(fmt_p(chisq.test(table(DSN$CVPK))$p.value),
            fmt_p(fisher.test(EXCL_TAB)$p.value),
            fmt_p(chisq.test(table(ANALYSIS$CVPK))$p.value),
            fmt_p(t.test(AGEEXAM ~ CVPK, data = ANALYSIS)$p.value),
            fmt_p(chisq.test(ANALYSIS$CVPK, ANALYSIS$MVF, correct = FALSE)$p.value)))

  cat("\n====", "Summary Table", "====\n")
  print(knitr::kable(TAB))
  invisible(TAB)  
   
   

   
   
   
   
   
   
  
}
```

## D. Variable Names and Alignment



The child self-report and parent assessment versions of the HiPIC contain 144 corresponding items, but the questions are presented in different sequences. The child version distributes items across domains and facets, whereas the parent version groups related items together.

To ensure consistency in scoring, parent responses were mapped to their corresponding child-item positions using the original questionnaire content. The resulting datasets share a common item-numbering system, permitting application of De Fruyt's scoring key to both respondent groups.

The original imported datasets were preserved without modification.



```{r child-parent-crosswalk}

HIPIC_CROSSWALK <- read.csv( "/Volumes/FDrive/AllQsbyQ/HIPIC/HiPIC_Questionnaire_Concordance_144.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE )

dim(HIPIC_CROSSWALK)
names(HIPIC_CROSSWALK)


library(sqldf)



PARENT_ALIGNED <-

sqldf("  select Q_NEW,
                concat('P', substr(CHILD_PREPEND,2)) as PARENT_PREPEND,
                PARENT_Q_WORDING,
                BNS_NAME_C,
                BNS_NAME_P,
                Q_ORIG
                
                
        from 
        
        
        ( select    PARENT_PREPEND,
                    PARENT_Q_WORDING,
                    BNS_NAME_P,
                    Q as Q_ORIG
          
          from HIPIC_CROSSWALK )  a inner join
        
         (select CHILD_PREPEND,
                 BNS_NAME_C,
                 Q as Q_NEW
                  
          from HIPIC_CROSSWALK)  b  on a.BNS_NAME_P = b.BNS_NAME_C  " )
```

## E. Item-Level Reverse Scoring

The scoring key provided by DeFruyt identifies the questions along each domain/facet that require reverse scoring.


``` {r reverse-secoring}




#Items identified as requireing reverse scoring in DeFruyt's key (questions are moving in opposite directions from other questions in the instrument):


REVERSE_ITEMS <- c(  1, 5, 8, 16, 17, 20, 27, 35, 37, 41,
                     42, 44, 49, 50, 53, 55, 60, 62, 63, 79,
                     80, 84, 87, 89, 99, 103, 107, 110, 120,
                     121, 122, 124, 129, 138, 139, 143  )



# use an ACROSS statement to compute a revers score for the items in the REVERSE_ITEMS vector


CHILD_REVERSED <-CHILD %>% mutate(across( starts_with( paste0("C", REVERSE_ITEMS, "_")),
                    function(x) 6 - x )
                        )

PARENT_REVERSED <-PARENT %>% mutate(across( starts_with( paste0("P", REVERSE_ITEMS, "_")),
              function(x) 6 - x )
                  )          




write.csv(PARENT_REVERSED,
          "PARENT_REVERSED.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)


write.csv(PARENT,
          "PARENT.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)


# Assign questions for each facet to unique vector

#Emotional Stability

ES_ANX <- c(4, 22, 40, 58, 76, 94, 112, 130)
ES_CON <- c(9, 27, 45, 63, 81, 99, 117, 135)

#Extroversion

EX_ENE <- c(15, 33, 51, 69, 87, 105, 123, 141)
EX_EXP <- c(6, 24, 42, 60, 78, 96, 114, 132)
EX_OPT <- c(11,29, 47,65, 83, 101, 119, 137)
EX_SHY <- c(1, 19, 37, 55, 73, 91, 109, 127)

#Imagination 

IM_CRE <- c(5, 23, 41, 59, 77, 95, 113, 131)
IM_INT <- c(14, 32, 50, 68,86, 104, 122, 140)
IM_CUR <- c(10, 28, 46, 64, 82, 100, 118, 136)

#Benevolence

BE_ALT <- c(18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108, 126, 144)
BE_DOM <- c(16, 34, 52, 70, 88, 106, 124, 142)
BE_EGO <- c(2, 20, 38, 56, 74, 92, 110, 128)
BE_COM <- c(12, 30, 48, 66, 84, 102, 120, 138)
BE_IRR <- c(7, 25, 43, 61, 79, 97, 115, 133)

#Conscientiousness

CO_CNC <- c(13, 31, 49, 67, 85, 103, 121, 139)
CO_PER <- c(17, 35, 53, 71, 89, 107, 125, 143)
CO_ORD <- c(8, 26, 44, 62, 80, 98, 116, 134)
CO_ACH <- c(3, 21, 39, 57, 75, 93, 111, 129)





# Compute dacets & domain scores based on DeFruyt's formulas 


# Since code is similar except for the files called, the files creatd and the vaiable prefix, consider a simple function  -not quite a SAS do loop, but still more efficient that duplicate blocks of code


#SCORE HIPIC FUNCTION



score_hipic <- function(DATA, PREFIX) {

  DATA %>%
  mutate(
    ES_ANX = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, ES_ANX, "_"))) ),
    ES_CON = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, ES_CON, "_"))) ),
    
        # Emotional Stability
        ES = (48 - ES_ANX) + ES_CON,
    
    EX_ENE = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, EX_ENE, "_"))) ),
    EX_EXP = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, EX_EXP, "_"))) ),
    EX_OPT = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, EX_OPT, "_"))) ),
    EX_SHY = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, EX_SHY, "_"))) ),
    
      # Extraversion
      EX = EX_ENE + EX_EXP + EX_OPT + (48 - EX_SHY),  
    
    
    IM_CRE = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, IM_CRE, "_"))) ),
    IM_INT = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, IM_INT, "_"))) ),
    IM_CUR = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, IM_CUR, "_"))) ),

      # Imagination
      IM = IM_CRE + IM_INT + IM_CUR,

    
    BE_ALT = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, BE_ALT, "_"))) ),
    BE_DOM = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, BE_DOM, "_"))) ),
    BE_EGO = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, BE_EGO, "_"))) ),
    BE_COM = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, BE_COM, "_"))) ),
    BE_IRR = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, BE_IRR, "_"))) ),
    
      # Benevolence
      BE = BE_ALT + (48 - BE_DOM) + (48 - BE_EGO) + BE_COM + (48 - BE_IRR),
    
    CO_CNC = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, CO_CNC, "_"))) ),
    CO_PER = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, CO_PER, "_"))) ),
    CO_ORD = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, CO_ORD, "_"))) ),
    CO_ACH = rowSums( select(., starts_with(paste0(PREFIX, CO_ACH, "_"))) ),
  
    # Conscientiousness
    CO = CO_CNC + CO_PER + CO_ORD + CO_ACH  
    
    
  ) %>% select( SG, ID4:MVF, AGEEXAM, ES_ANX:CO)

}





CHILD_SCORED  <- score_hipic(CHILD_REVERSED, "C")
PARENT_SCORED <- score_hipic(PARENT_REVERSED, "P")








write.csv(PARENT_SCORED,
          "QC",
          row.names = FALSE)








# Prepare a Facets Crosswalk summary for Slide Deck if needed.

    FACETS <- list(
      Anxiety = ES_ANX, `Self-Confidence` = ES_CON,
      Energy = EX_ENE, Expressiveness = EX_EXP, Optimism = EX_OPT, Shyness = EX_SHY,
      Creativity = IM_CRE, Intellect = IM_INT, Curiosity = IM_CUR,
      Altruism = BE_ALT, Dominance = BE_DOM, Egocentrism = BE_EGO,
      Compliance = BE_COM, Irritability = BE_IRR,
      Concentration = CO_CNC, Perseverance = CO_PER, Order = CO_ORD,
      `Achievement Motivation` = CO_ACH)
    
    FACET_KEY <- stack(FACETS)   # one row per item: values = item #, ind = facet name
    nrow(FACET_KEY)              # check: should be 144
    
    
    
    XWALK_SLIDE <- PARENT_ALIGNED %>%
      arrange(Q_ORIG) %>%
      slice(1:16) %>%
      left_join(FACET_KEY, by = c("Q_NEW" = "values")) %>%
      transmute(`Parent #`       = Q_ORIG,
                `Parent Wording` = PARENT_Q_WORDING,
                `Child #`        = Q_NEW,
                `SAS Varname`       = BNS_NAME_C,
                Facet            = as.character(ind))
    
    XWALK_SLIDE                               # look before saving
    saveRDS(XWALK_SLIDE, "tab_crosswalk.rds")









```


## E.  Find mean differences between nutritional groups across all domains and facets.  Produce results separately for males and females.


``` {r mean-diffs}



#BEGIN FUNCTION DEFINITION




hipic_mean_diffs <- function(DATA) {



options(scipen = 999)
cat("\014")

analysis_vars <- names(DATA)[
  match("ES_ANX", names(DATA)):ncol(DATA)]

runs <- c(0,1,2)



for (variable in analysis_vars) {
  print(variable)
}

BASE <- data.frame()



for ( sex in runs  ) {


for (variable in analysis_vars) {
  
  
  test_formula <- reformulate("CVPK", response = variable)
  
  test_result <- misty::test.welch(
    test_formula,
    # data = DATA[DATA$MVF == sex, ],
    data = DATA[ if (sex < 2) DATA$MVF == sex else TRUE, ],
    descript = TRUE
  )
  
  r<- test_result$result
  con <- r$group == 0
  mal <- r$group == 1
  
  print(variable)
  print(r$t)
  print(r$pval)
  
  
  x <- DATA[[variable]][
        DATA$CVPK %in% c(0, 1) &
        !is.na(DATA[[variable]]) &
                        (if (sex < 2) DATA$MVF == sex else TRUE)
  ]
  
  
#   if(sex <2) {
# 
# 
#      x <- DATA[[variable]][DATA$CVPK %in% c(0,1) &
#                                   DATA$MVF == sex &
#                                     !is.na(DATA[[variable]])]  }
# 
# else {
# 
#       x <- DATA[[variable]][DATA$CVPK %in% c(0,1) &
#                 !is.na(DATA[[variable]])]   }
  
  
#  x <- DATA$ES_ANX[ DATA$CVPK %in% c(0, 1) &  !is.na(DATA$ES_ANX) ]
 
  
   
  temp <- data.frame(
    MODEL = sprintf("%02d", sex   ),
    VARNAME  = variable,
    
    `_STAT_` = c("MEAN", "STD", "N",
                 "TTEST WELCH", "PVALUE"),
    
    MAL = c(r$m[mal], r$sd[mal], r$n[mal],
            NA_real_, NA_real_),
    
    CON = c(r$m[con], r$sd[con], r$n[con],
            NA_real_, NA_real_),
    
    ALL = c(mean(x), sd(x), length(x),
            r$t[!is.na(r$t)],
            r$pval[!is.na(r$pval)]),
    
    check.names = FALSE  )
  
  BASE <- rbind(BASE, temp)
  
  
}

}
    return(BASE)
}



BASEC <- hipic_mean_diffs(CHILD_SCORED)
BASEP <- hipic_mean_diffs(PARENT_SCORED)

```

##F. Examine the questions on both surveys that had the highest concentration of answers along any one response.


``` {r top-questions}


#DEFINE FUNCTION



hipic_quest_distrib <- function(DATA) {
  
  

lastcol <- length(colnames(DATA))
lastcol

# 1. Store the question names in their original column order

question_names <- names(DATA) %>%
  .[grepl("^[PC][0-9]+_", .)]

#2. Store questions that were reverse scored

revscored <- c(
  27, 63, 99, 87, 42, 60, 1, 37, 5, 41, 50, 122, 16, 124,
  20, 110, 120, 138, 79, 103, 121, 139, 17, 35, 53, 89, 107,
  143, 8, 44, 62, 80, 129,49, 55, 84 )



#3. find quesiton prefix value

prefix <- substr( grep("^[PC]1_", colnames(DATA), value = TRUE), 1, 1)




#as.integer(sub("^P([0-9]+)_.*$", "\\1", "P5_IMAGINE_haslittleimagination"))



x<-
  DATA %>% 
pivot_longer( cols=  matches( paste0("^", prefix, "[0-9]") ),
              names_to = "QUESTIONS",
              values_to = "RESPONSE") %>% 
  
  mutate(  KEYNUM = sprintf("Q%03d",  as.integer(sub(     paste0("^", prefix, "([0-9]+)_.*$"), "\\1",  QUESTIONS))) ,
           RS = case_when( as.integer(sub(      paste0("^", prefix, "([0-9]+)_.*$"), "\\1", QUESTIONS)) %in% revscored ~ 'Y', TRUE ~ "") ,
    
    
           # KEYNUM = sprintf("Q%03d",  as.integer(sub("^P([0-9]+)_.*$", "\\1",  QUESTIONS))) ,
           # RS = case_when( as.integer(sub("^P([0-9]+)_.*$", "\\1", QUESTIONS)) %in% revscored ~ 'Y', TRUE ~ "") ,
           
          POSITION = sprintf("Q%03d", match(QUESTIONS, question_names)) 
          
                ) %>%
```

```{r fa-setup, include=F}

# 144 items per sample (reverse-scored, imputed)
C_ITEMS <- CHILD_REVERSED  %>% select(last_col(offset = 143):last_col())
P_ITEMS <- PARENT_REVERSED %>% select(last_col(offset = 143):last_col())

# item-level eigenvalues (correlation matrix)
EV_C <- eigen(cor(C_ITEMS))$values
EV_P <- eigen(cor(P_ITEMS))$values

# 18 facets per sample (domain totals excluded)
C_FACETS <- CHILD_SCORED  %>% select(matches("^(ES|EX|IM|BE|CO)_"))
P_FACETS <- PARENT_SCORED %>% select(matches("^(ES|EX|IM|BE|CO)_"))

# item-level factor solutions used by later chunks
FA5_C      <- psych::fa(C_ITEMS, nfactors = 5, fm = "minres", rotate = "varimax")
FA5_PVMAX  <- psych::fa(P_ITEMS, nfactors = 5, fm = "minres", rotate = "varimax")
FA5_CNOROT <- psych::fa(C_ITEMS, nfactors = 5, fm = "minres", rotate = "none")
FA5_PNOROT <- psych::fa(P_ITEMS, nfactors = 5, fm = "minres", rotate = "none")
FA2I_C     <- psych::fa(C_ITEMS, nfactors = 2, fm = "minres", rotate = "varimax")
FA2I_P     <- psych::fa(P_ITEMS, nfactors = 2, fm = "minres", rotate = "varimax")
```

```{r scree-plots-children}
set.seed(2026)

png("images/scree_items_child.png", width = 1400, height = 1100, res = 200)

     xlab = "Factor", ylab = "Eigenvalue", main = "")
lines(1:20, PA_C$fa.sim[1:20], lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topright", c("Actual data", "Random data (parallel analysis)"),
       col = c("#006cc5", "grey40"), lty = c(1, 2), pch = c(19, NA), bty = "n")
dev.off()



EIG_C <- tibble(Factor     = 1:10,
                Eigenvalue = round(EV_C[1:10], 2),
                Difference = round(EV_C[1:10] - EV_C[2:11], 2),
                Proportion = round(EV_C[1:10] / 144, 3),
                Cumulative = round(cumsum(EV_C)[1:10] / 144, 3))
saveRDS(EIG_C, "eig_child.rds")





# loadings, with columns put in size order and renamed F1–F5
LV <- unclass(FA5_C$loadings)[, c("MR1", "MR2", "MR3", "MR5", "MR4")]
colnames(LV) <- paste0("F", 1:5)

LOAD_C <- as_tibble(LV) %>%
  mutate(Q       = as.integer(sub("^C(\\d+)_.*", "\\1", rownames(LV))),
         Primary = apply(abs(LV), 1, which.max),     # factor each item loads on most
         Max     = apply(abs(LV), 1, max)) %>%       # that item's largest loading
  left_join(HIPIC_CROSSWALK %>% select(Q, Item = CHILD_Q_WORDING), by = "Q") %>%
  arrange(Primary, desc(Max))                        # group by factor, strongest first

TOP_C <- LOAD_C %>%
  group_by(Primary) %>% slice_head(n = 10) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(F1:F5, ~ ifelse(abs(.x) < .30, "", sprintf("%.2f", .x)))) %>%
  select(`#` = Q, Item, F1:F5)

saveRDS(TOP_C, "top_load_child.rds")


LOAD_C %>% filter(Max >= .30) %>% count(Primary)   # items whose best loading is ≥ .30, by factor
sum(LOAD_C$Max < .30)                              # items below .30 on every factor



#curious about Alphas




# High alphas here would be easy to get and easy to over-read. Alpha above .70 is a reasonable minimum. It isn’t evidence that the factors are real traits, and in this dataset there are four reasons it would mislead:
# 
# The items were chosen because they correlate in this sample. Building scales from this sample’s loadings and then computing alpha on the same sample is circular: the alpha is inflated by the same chance patterns that shaped the loadings. A meaningful alpha has to come from an independent sample.
# Alpha rises with the number of items. F1 has 30-plus items loading above .30. With that many items, alpha will almost certainly exceed .90 even if the items are only modestly related, so a high value says little.
# High alpha doesn’t mean one trait. Alpha measures how consistently items move together, not why. F1 (overall positive self-description) and F2 (the agreement-direction pattern) hold together largely because of how children answer. Both would probably produce excellent alphas that reflect response style rather than personality.
# At n = 74, alpha itself is imprecise. The confidence intervals around it are wide.

# All five factors are internally consistent in this sample (α = .72–.96). Because the scales were derived from the same 74 children, these alphas are optimistic, and the highest values belong to the two factors carrying the most response-style variance. They’re strong candidates to confirm in an independent sample.” That keeps her momentum towards a paper, but points it at the confirmation step rather than the write-up.



ALPHAS_C <- sapply(1:5, function(k) {
  q     <- LOAD_C %>% filter(Primary == k, Max >= .30) %>% pull(Q)
  items <- CHILD_REVERSED %>% select(starts_with(paste0("C", q, "_")))
  psych::alpha(items, check.keys = TRUE)$total$raw_alpha
})

round(ALPHAS_C, 2)


sapply(1:5, function(k) LOAD_C %>% filter(Primary == k, Max >= .30) %>% nrow())   # items per factor

sapply(1:5, function(k) {
  q     <- LOAD_C %>% filter(Primary == k, Max >= .30) %>% pull(Q)
  items <- CHILD_REVERSED %>% select(starts_with(paste0("C", q, "_")))
  psych::alpha(items, check.keys = TRUE)$total$average_r
})
```

#  Attempt to write a function that runs over the PARENTS and CHILD reverse scored datasets but allows you to key in paramenters for rotation desired, number of factors



```{ r function-definition-full-run}



run_fa <- function(DSN, NFACT, ROT = "none", METHOD = "minres", SORT = "factor") {
  
  # >>> EXCEL DESTINATION: change this line to write somewhere else <<<
  
  FILE <- "/Users/Kevin/OneDrive/Documents/Excel/HiPIC FA Tests.xlsx"
  
  
  
  
  # 1. The 144 items are always the last 144 columns
  ITEMS  <- DSN %>% select(last_col(offset = 143):last_col())
  PREFIX <- substr(names(ITEMS)[1], 1, 1)                 # "C" or "P"
  
  # 2. Run the analysis: PCA (SAS PROC FACTOR default) or a true factor analysis
  FA <- if (METHOD == "pca") {
    psych::principal(ITEMS, nfactors = NFACT, rotate = ROT)
  } else {
    psych::fa(ITEMS, nfactors = NFACT, fm = METHOD, rotate = ROT)
  }
  
  # 3. Loadings: factors in size order, renamed F1, F2, ...
  L <- unclass(FA$loadings)
  L <- L[, order(-colSums(L^2)), drop = FALSE]
  colnames(L) <- paste0("F", 1:NFACT)
  
  # 4. Item wording: children from the crosswalk, parents from the realignment table
  WORD <- if (PREFIX == "C") {
    HIPIC_CROSSWALK %>% select(Q, Wording = CHILD_Q_WORDING)
  } else {
    PARENT_ALIGNED %>% select(Q = Q_NEW, Wording = PARENT_Q_WORDING)
  }
  
  # 5. Build the table: fixed columns first, loadings last
  OUT <- tibble(Question = as.integer(sub("^[CP](\\d+)_.*", "\\1", rownames(L))),
                SAS_Name = sub("^[CP]\\d+_([^_]+)_.*", "\\1", rownames(L))) %>%
    left_join(WORD, by = c("Question" = "Q")) %>%
    mutate(Reversed = ifelse(Question %in% REVERSE_ITEMS, "Y", ""),
           Primary  = paste0("F", apply(abs(L), 1, which.max)),
           h2       = round(FA$communality, 3),
           .Max     = apply(abs(L), 1, max)) %>%
    bind_cols(as_tibble(round(L, 3)))
  
  # 6. Sort: by home factor (strongest first), or by item number
  OUT <- if (SORT == "factor") arrange(OUT, Primary, desc(.Max)) else arrange(OUT, Question)
  OUT <- select(OUT, -.Max)
  
  # 6b. Append the variance-explained row at the end
  VAR_ROW <- tibble(Wording = "VAR EXPLAINED") %>%
    bind_cols(as_tibble(t(round(colSums(L^2) / ncol(ITEMS), 3))))
  OUT <- bind_rows(OUT, VAR_ROW)
  
  # 7. Print the headline in the Console
  cat("\n====", deparse(substitute(DSN)), "|", NFACT, "factors |", ROT, "|", METHOD, "====\n")
  print(VAR_ROW %>% select(-Wording))
  
  
  # 8. Write the table to its own sheet in the workbook (skipped with a message if it can't)
  tryCatch({
    SHEET <- paste(PREFIX, NFACT, ROT, METHOD, sep = "_")      # e.g. "P_5_varimax_minres"
    
    wb <- if (file.exists(FILE)) openxlsx::loadWorkbook(FILE) else openxlsx::createWorkbook()
    if (!SHEET %in% names(wb)) openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, SHEET)
    
    openxlsx::deleteData(wb, SHEET, cols = 1:30, rows = 1:300, gridExpand = TRUE)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, SHEET, OUT)
    openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, FILE, overwrite = TRUE)
    
    cat("Written to sheet", SHEET, "in", basename(FILE), "\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Excel export skipped:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
  
  # 9. Hand back the table (and the full FA result) for inspection
  invisible(list(loadings = OUT, fa = FA))
}




R1 <- run_fa(CHILD_REVERSED, 5, 'varimax', "minres")
View(R1$loadings)


```


# Factor analysis on a questionnaire this unwieldy (144-items) across this few subjects my not be reliable — the correlation matrix is singular, so it cannot be inverted, and standard adequacy tests cannot be computed.  Is a Facet-level analysis worth taking a look at?  Test on parents only.


```{r scree-plots-parents-facets}

lines(1:18, PA_PF$fa.sim, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topright", c("Actual data", "Random data (parallel analysis)"),
       col = c("#006cc5", "grey40"), lty = c(1, 2), pch = c(19, NA), bty = "n")
dev.off()

EIG_PF <- tibble(Factor     = 1:10,

                 Difference = round(EV_PF[1:10] - EV_PF[2:11], 2),
```

```{r parent_two-factor-facets}
colnames(L) <- paste0("F", 1:ncol(L))

# readable labels for the 18 facet codes and 5 domains
FACET_NAMES  <- c(ES_ANX = "Anxiety", ES_CON = "Self-Confidence",
                  EX_ENE = "Energy", EX_EXP = "Expressiveness", EX_OPT = "Optimism", EX_SHY = "Shyness",
                  IM_CRE = "Creativity", IM_INT = "Intellect", IM_CUR = "Curiosity",
                  BE_ALT = "Altruism", BE_DOM = "Dominance", BE_EGO = "Egocentrism",
```
